Hi Karthik,

We're working through the security questionnaire for our pilot with Redwood and have a few clarifying questions about default data retention. The questionnaire asks for explicit statements we can give to our legal team about what your hosted API stores by default. Specifically:

- Do you retain the full request payload (prompts, system messages, function call arguments) and the model-generated outputs by default? If so, for how long?
- Are partial/streamed tokens treated differently from final outputs?
- Do you persist derived artifacts (e.g., embeddings, reranks, cached KV/response caches) by default?
- Is residency of stored items (US vs EU) configurable per account, or only for enterprise/PV deployments?

We need short, precise answers we can paste into the questionnaire + any attachments you can share (retention summary, DPA language, SOC2 evidence or a pointer to it).

Attached is the questionnaire workbook (section "Data Retention"). Can we have a written reply by EOD tomorrow? If it's easier, happy to schedule a 30m call.

Jane — thanks for the clear questions and the workbook. See concise answers below (bullet form for easy insertion into your questionnaire). I'll also attach our short "Redwood Default Retention Summary" PDF and loop in Security for any legal wording tweaks.

• Default hosted API behavior (out-of-the-box): we persist request payloads (including prompts, system messages, and function-call inputs) and model-generated outputs for 30 days to support debugging, abuse investigation, and quality regression detection.

• Streaming tokens: intermediate streamed tokens are not persisted as separate artifacts beyond the normal request/response record; the final assembled output is what is retained.

• Derived artifacts: embeddings and customer-created artifacts are NOT stored by Redwood by default unless explicitly enabled (for example, customers who turn on the embeddings store or long-term caching). Ephemeral caches (KV caches used to accelerate ongoing sessions) are treated as transient and are rotated/purged automatically; these are not retained in long-term logs by default.

• Residency: For hosted (multi-tenant) customers, logs default to the region where the account was provisioned (US or EU). Enterprise/Dedicated customers can request contractual residency assurances (logs kept only in customer-chosen region) or deploy via Redwood Private which keeps logs under customer control.

Options we offer: 30-day default can be shortened via account settings / DPA; enterprise agreements can pin deletion windows or opt for no-log operation (redact-on-ingress) if required. Private/Dedicated modes offer additional controls; we'll summarize choices in the attached PDF.

Next steps: I can (1) provide a one-page statement you can paste into the questionnaire, (2) schedule a short call with Security if you need legal language, or (3) provide SOC2 snapshot links and DPA examples. Which do you prefer?

—Karthik

Karthik / Priyom — quick internal note on formal wording before we send anything to Acme. I suggest we avoid terms that could be misread (e.g., 'we persist' vs 'we retain accessible logs') and be explicit about what customers can request via the Console or contract. Draft suggested paragraph below (feel free to trim for the questionnaire):

"By default, Redwood's hosted API retains request/response records (including prompts, system messages, and generated outputs) for 30 days from the time of ingestion. Intermediate streaming tokens are not stored separately; the final response is what is retained. Derived artifacts (such as embeddings or model-derived indices) are not retained by default unless a customer enables a storage feature for those artifacts. Customers in the EU or other regions have their account logs stored in the region selected at provisioning; Enterprise and Dedicated customers may contractually require alternate residency and customized deletion windows. Private deployments keep telemetry and logs under customer control."

Also add: for enterprise customers we can offer a 7-day purge for ephemeral caches and a separate option for "redact-on-ingress" that prevents storage of raw prompts/outputs in our control plane. We should attach the DPA template snippet if Acme asks for contract language.

Priyom — can you confirm the ephemeral cache purge timeframe (I think our service rotates caches every 48 hours and tombstones are fully removed within 7 days) so we can be precise?

-Lauren

Redwood Default Retention (hosted API):
- Request payloads (including prompts, system messages, and function-call inputs) and final model-generated outputs are retained in accessible logs for 30 days from ingestion.
- Intermediate streamed tokens are not retained as separate artifacts; the final assembled response is what is captured.
- Derived artifacts (embeddings, customer-created indices) are NOT persisted by default unless the customer explicitly enables that storage feature.
- Ephemeral runtime caches (e.g., KV/session caches used to speed inference) are rotated regularly and tombstoned entries are fully removed within 7 days; these are not part of long-term accessible logs by default.
- Residency: Hosted accounts are provisioned to a default region (US or EU) and logs are stored in that region. Enterprise/Dedicated/Private deployments support contractual residency guarantees or customer-controlled storage.

If Acme requires: we support shorter retention windows (e.g., 7-day) or redact-on-ingress (preventing storage of raw request payloads) as contract options for enterprise customers.
